title: Machine Design
description: Machine Design covers stress and failure theories, fatigue, shafts, bearings, gears, belt and chain drives, clutches and brakes, joints, springs, and the design process through projects, tolerancing, manufacturing, optimization, and validation.

topics.title: Stress Analysis and Failure Theories
topics.description: Machine design begins by predicting whether parts can carry loads without yielding, fracturing, buckling, or otherwise failing in service.

children.title: Load paths and free-body models
children.description: Students learn to reduce real components to force and moment models that can be analyzed.

children.title: Axial, bending, torsional, and transverse loads
Stress states
children.description: Machine elements often experience combined normal and shear stresses, so stress transformation matters.

children.title: Static failure theories
children.description: Failure theories translate multiaxial stress states into design criteria.

children.title: Factors of safety
children.description: Safety factors account for uncertainty in loads, materials, modeling, and consequences.

topics.title: Fatigue and Infinite-Life Design
topics.description: Many machine parts fail after repeated loading even when peak stresses are below static strength. Fatigue design teaches students how to design for life.

children.title: Fatigue mechanisms
children.description: Students learn why cracks initiate and grow under cyclic stress.

children.title: S-N curves and endurance limits
children.description: S-N data connect alternating stress to expected life.

children.title: Mean stress corrections
children.description: Real fatigue loads often combine alternating and mean stress.

children.title: Infinite-life and variable-loading design
children.description: Students learn to size components for long life under realistic loading histories.

topics.title: Shafts and Shaft Components
topics.description: Shafts transmit power and support rotating elements. Their design combines stress, deflection, fatigue, keyways, shoulders, bearings, and assembly constraints.

children.title: Power transmission in shafts
children.description: Students connect torque, speed, power, and geometry.

children.title: Shaft layout
children.description: Layout choices determine where loads enter, where bearings sit, and where stress concentrations arise.

children.title: Deflection and stiffness
children.description: Shafts must be strong enough and stiff enough for gears, bearings, seals, and alignment.

children.title: Fatigue design of shafts
children.description: Rotating shafts often see fully reversed bending and steady torsion.

topics.title: Bearings (Rolling and Journal)
topics.description: Bearings support motion while controlling friction, load, alignment, life, and lubrication. Design selection matters for reliability and maintenance.

children.title: Rolling-element bearing types
children.description: Students learn how bearing geometry changes load capacity and application fit.

children.title: Bearing life and selection
children.description: Bearing ratings let designers estimate life under load and speed.

children.title: Journal bearings
children.description: Journal bearings rely on fluid films and are common in high-load or high-speed systems.

children.title: Mounting and failure modes
children.description: A good bearing choice can fail if mounting, lubrication, or alignment is wrong.

topics.title: Gears (Spur, Helical, Bevel)
topics.description: Gears transmit motion and power with controlled speed ratios. Gear design balances tooth geometry, stress, wear, noise, and manufacturability.

children.title: Gear terminology and geometry
children.description: Students learn the vocabulary and geometry needed to specify gear pairs.

children.title: Spur and helical gears
children.description: Spur and helical gears are common parallel-shaft power transmission elements.

children.title: Bevel gears
children.description: Bevel gears transmit power between intersecting shafts.

children.title: Gear trains and design tradeoffs
children.description: Gear systems require ratio planning and packaging decisions.

topics.title: Belt and Chain Drives
topics.description: Belts and chains provide flexible power transmission options when shafts are separated or when shock, cost, or alignment considerations matter.

children.title: Belt drive types
children.description: Belt choice affects slip, power capacity, maintenance, and packaging.

children.title: Belt-drive design
children.description: Students learn the force and power relationships behind belt selection.

children.title: Chain drives
children.description: Chains provide positive drive without slip but introduce polygonal action and lubrication needs.

children.title: Selection tradeoffs
children.description: Belts and chains are chosen by balancing cost, precision, noise, efficiency, and service conditions.

topics.title: Clutches and Brakes
topics.description: Clutches and brakes control engagement, motion, and stopping. Their design involves friction, heat generation, wear, actuation, and safety.

children.title: Friction fundamentals
children.description: Students learn how friction transmits torque and dissipates energy.

children.title: Uniform wear and uniform pressure assumptions
Clutch types
children.description: Clutches engage and disengage power transmission.

children.title: Brake types
children.description: Brakes convert kinetic energy into heat and must stop motion reliably.

children.title: Thermal and wear considerations
children.description: Friction devices are limited by heat, wear, and material behavior.

topics.title: Bolted and Welded Joints
topics.description: Joints are common failure points. Students learn how fasteners and welds carry load, maintain preload, and create manufacturable assemblies.

children.title: Bolted joint mechanics
children.description: Preload changes how a joint carries external load and resists separation.

children.title: Bolted joint failure modes
children.description: Fasteners can fail through many paths, so design checks must be systematic.

children.title: Welded joint types
children.description: Weld geometry determines load path and inspection needs.

children.title: Weld design and quality
children.description: Welds require design, process, and inspection thinking.

topics.title: Springs
topics.description: Springs store energy, provide force, absorb shock, and control motion. Spring design combines stress, deflection, fatigue, and manufacturability.

children.title: Spring types
children.description: Different spring forms suit different force, motion, and packaging needs.

children.title: Helical compression spring design
children.description: Compression springs are a core machine-design example because stress and deflection are tightly coupled.

children.title: Spring materials and fatigue
children.description: Springs frequently see cyclic loading and must be designed for life.

children.title: Spring selection and application
children.description: Students learn when to design a spring and when to select a catalog part.

topics.title: Design Projects
topics.description: Projects integrate analysis, component selection, modeling, drawings, cost, manufacturing, testing, and communication into a realistic design workflow.

children.title: Problem definition
children.description: A good project begins with a clear statement of what the machine must do and under what constraints.

children.title: Concept generation and selection
children.description: Students practice creating alternatives and selecting based on evidence rather than preference.

children.title: Detailed design and documentation
children.description: Project work forces students to turn analysis into drawings, BOMs, and buildable designs.

children.title: Prototype, test, and iterate
children.description: Testing reveals whether the design works and where assumptions were wrong.

topics.title: Design Process, Requirements, and Decision-Making
topics.description: This added synthesis topic makes the course more than a catalog of components by teaching students how design problems are framed and decisions are justified.

children.title: Requirements and stakeholder needs
children.description: Students learn to translate vague needs into measurable design requirements.

children.title: Concept development
children.description: Concept work keeps students from jumping too quickly to the first workable mechanism.

children.title: Decision methods
children.description: Decision tools make tradeoffs visible and defensible.

children.title: Design reviews and documentation
children.description: Professional machine design depends on communicating assumptions, calculations, and evidence.

topics.title: Tolerancing, Manufacturing, Optimization, and Validation
topics.description: This added topic connects machine-element calculations to real production, assembly, performance improvement, and verification.

children.title: Tolerancing and fits
children.description: Tolerances determine whether parts assemble, move, and perform as intended.

children.title: Design for manufacturing and assembly
children.description: Design choices should fit available manufacturing processes and assembly constraints.

children.title: Machining, casting, forming, and additive manufacturing
Optimization formulation
children.description: Optimization helps students improve designs subject to constraints.

children.title: Testing and validation
children.description: Validation closes the loop between predicted performance and actual behavior.
